A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel multi-agent kernel approximation framework that allows the agents distributedly estimate the kernel function, and thereby, achieve communication-efficient decentralized learning without directly exchanging the local data or parameters.

, we propose a novel multi-agent kernel approximation technique that allows the distributed agents to learn overparameterized models (such as the NTK models) without sharing any local data or model parameters.

the proposed multi-agent kernel approximation framework is the first to achieve communication-efficient distributed learning for overparameterized problems, and is also the first to demonstrate the benefits of overparamterization in the decentralized setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

overparameterized problems are amenable to distributed optimization without the need to exchange local data or parameters, and that the proposed framework provides an efficient and practical solution to distributed learning for such problems.

, for overparameterized problems with a small number of local samples per agent, the agents do not need to exchange any local data or model parameters in order to achieve the same performance as centralized optimization.
the proposed framework is communication-efficient, and it can achieve the minimax optimal generalisation performance for a broad class of kernel methods.
